digest.component_or_area: Jira bridge reconciler — duplicate comment cleanup
propositions: Phase 1 removal of marker-bearing bridge-echo duplicates deliberately skipped 836 unmarked truncated comments across REB-1567, REB-1931, and REB-2605 because they lacked the authoritative reconciler marker, but they are bot-authored duplicates at exactly 32767 rendered characters ending in _TRUNCATION_SUFFIX that must be removed.

The marker is missing because outbound truncation appends the marker after the body, causing the 32767-character cut to remove it before persistence, making the loop-breaker inert for over-length comments; this defect is filed separately and not the scope of this cleanup ticket.

Candidates for deletion must satisfy all four conditions conjunctively: bot accountId match, exactly 32767 rendered character length, text ending with _TRUNCATION_SUFFIX, and absence of RECONCILER_MARKER; any comment failing any condition is not deleted.
A fresh dry run must be executed and inspected before any deletion to confirm the candidate count per issue, with pre-deletion backup of full comment payloads gated on count verification.

The keep-one rule for phase 2 retains the OLDEST copy of each distinct normalized body; after the bridge re-enables and the final sweep occurs, the rule must invert to keep only the copy whose id appears in the binding store's comment_ids map.

The sequencing hazard requires cleaning before bridge re-enablement, followed by a single re-post per distinct truncated comment on the first pass, then a final sweep; divergence from the expected one re-post per body is a signal to stop and re-examine.
